edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Praefatio nostra viam erranti demonstrat; Respectumque bonum, cum venerit saeculi meta; Aeternum fieri: quod discredunt inscia corda: Ego similiter erravi tempore multo, Fana prosequendo, parentibus insciis ipsis. Abstuli me tandem inde, legendo de Lege. Testificor Dominum; doleo: pro civica turba! Inscia quod perdit, pergens deos quaerere vanos. Ob ea perdoctus, ignaros instruo verum.
pass_a_gloss: Our introduction shows the way to the one who is erring; and a good regard, when the end of the age will have come; to be made eternal: which unknowing hearts disbelieve: I similarly erred for a long time, following idols, with my parents being unknowing themselves. I finally withdrew from there, reading from the Law. I testify to the Lord; I grieve for the civic crowd! Because it is unknowing, it is being destroyed, going to seek vain gods. On account of these things, having been thoroughly taught, I instruct the unknowing in the truth.

choices.why: turba can mean crowd or mob, and civica suggests a connection to the city or civic life
pergens is a present participle indicating ongoing action, and vanos means vain or empty

pass_b_english: This preface points the wanderer toward the right path, and toward a favorable outcome when the age reaches its end: becoming eternal, a truth that ignorant hearts refuse to believe. I myself wandered for a long time in the same way, chasing after idols, while my own parents were equally ignorant. I finally pulled myself out of that life by reading the Law. I call the Lord as my witness; I grieve for the city crowd! Because they do not know, they are perishing, chasing after empty gods. Since I have been thoroughly taught by these things, I now instruct the ignorant in the truth.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the nuances of 'inscia corda' (unknowing/ignorant hearts), 'Fana prosequendo' (following/chasing idols), and 'pergens deos quaerere vanos' (going to seek/chasing after vain/empty gods).
